finding.statement: A retained evidence writer must reject a pre-positioned hard-link output and preserve the shared inode bytes; no-overwrite evidence must cover aliasing by hard links as well as symbolic links and ordinary existing files.
finding.uncertainty: The fixture is committed but has not been observed in an authenticated checkout or GitHub Actions run through the available connector. Cross-platform hard-link creation permissions and filesystem behavior remain environment-specific.

primary_sources.title: Node.js File system documentation
primary_sources.relevance: Documents fsPromises.link, fsPromises.writeFile, and exclusive creation flags used by the fixture.

primary_sources.title: Linux open(2) manual page
primary_sources.relevance: Defines O_CREAT with O_EXCL failure when the named path already exists, which includes an existing hard-link directory entry.

implementation.test: exclusive manifest creation rejects a pre-positioned hard-link output without altering the shared inode

verification.claim_boundary: The commit proves the adversarial fixture exists. It does not prove the fixture passed on Linux, macOS, Windows, GitHub Actions, or a production host.

falsification_routes: Run node --test operations/tests/write-bound-vercel-authenticated-evidence-manifest.test.mjs in an authenticated checkout and retain stdout, exit status, Node version, operating system, filesystem type, and exact commit SHA.
Replace the exclusive-create flag with a nonexclusive write in a controlled branch; the hard-link fixture should detect mutation through both path aliases.
Execute on each supported platform and classify unsupported hard-link creation separately from a passed no-overwrite assertion.
design_implication: Treat filesystem path identity as potentially aliased. Retained evidence outputs must use exclusive creation and adversarial fixtures for ordinary files, symbolic links, and hard links before no-overwrite claims are promoted.
